transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Mostly sleep. It’s gotten… pretty unsteady. At first I’d be up after two or three hours and feel like I should start making plans, like I was ready to go. Now I’m awake before dawn, stomach tight, and I don’t feel rested at all.
During those times when you slept only two or three hours and still felt ready to go, did you feel unusually happy or high?

Yes. I mean… unusually optimistic, I suppose. For a few weeks it felt like nothing was really a problem, like I could handle anything. But if someone pushed back or questioned me, I’d get sharp with them pretty quickly.
During that period when you felt unusually optimistic, were you more active than usual?

Yes… more than usual. I couldn’t really sit still. I’d be up before sunrise, calling people, rewriting proposals, just moving from one thing to the next. It felt like there was an engine running inside me.
During that unusually energized period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work, financially, or in your relationships?

Yes… I suppose it did. My wife had to step in with the finances, and she’s been staying close to me… for safety, I guess. And I’ve stopped being reliable with the museum, the arts council, even seeing friends. It’s embarrassing.
During that energized period, did you have any experiences that others said were not real, such as hearing voices or having unusual beliefs?

I didn’t hear voices, no. But… I did have some pretty grand ideas. I honestly thought I could fix my retirement accounts, advise a few start-ups, and make the arts council into something much bigger. At the time it felt like my judgment was just… better than everyone else’s.
Did that unusually energized, overly optimistic period last for at least one week?
Yes. It was… much longer than a week. After the investment loss, I was like that for about five months, really. I wasn’t living like my usual retired self—everything was about trying to undo it.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yes. Since those plans fell apart, I’ve been… low, mostly withdrawn. It’s been about nine months now.
During this period of feeling low and withdrawn, have you had beliefs that other people said were not true?

Not… beliefs like that, exactly. I just keep thinking I’ve ruined everything. My wife’s security, our future. I replay that investment decision over and over and feel like I made a fool of myself after a lifetime of trying to be the responsible one.
Do you believe, as a fact, that you have destroyed your wife’s financial future?
I… I don’t know if I can call it a fact. But it feels true. I keep going over that decision and telling myself I ruined her security… like I made a fool of everything I tried to be.
During that energized period, were you absolutely certain you had special abilities or powers that other people said you did not have?

Yes… at the time I was sure my judgment was better than everyone else’s. I thought I could fix my retirement accounts, advise a few start-ups, even make the arts council into something much bigger. It sounds… inflated now, but then it felt completely certain.
